html:
The Nabataean Kingdom was an Arab kingdom in the deserts of today's Jordan, southern Syria, the Negev and northwest Arabia, with its capital at Petra. The Nabataeans first appear in history in 312 BCE, when they fought off an attack by one of Alexander's successors. Rome annexed the kingdom in 106 CE.

They grew rich on the caravan trade. Their land sat on the incense route from South Arabia to Gaza and Damascus, and they knew how to find and store water in the desert, with hidden cisterns and channels. At Petra they carved great tomb facades into the red rock, and at Hegra in Arabia they did the same.

Their kings, such as Aretas IV, dealt with the Seleucids, with Judaea and with Rome. Their writing, a form of Aramaic script, developed over time into the Arabic alphabet. In 106 CE Trajan made the kingdom the Roman province of Arabia Petraea.
